label: HMRC update · 2 November 2026
title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: five myths, and the next deadline on 7 February
summary: Quarterly updates are not tax returns and no tax is paid with them. What sole traders and landlords in MTD need to know before the third update.
body:
Making Tax Digital for Income Tax became mandatory on 6 April 2026 for sole traders and landlords with income over £50,000. The second quarterly update was due on 7 November 2026, and HMRC used the moment to clear up some common misunderstandings.

Five points HMRC has clarified

  • A quarterly update is not a tax return. It is a short summary of income and expenses sent through compatible software. There is no tax calculation and nothing to pay when you send it.
  • You do not need to call HMRC to check it arrived. Your submission history is in your HMRC online account or your software.
  • You do not need expensive software. There are several HMRC-recognised options, some free, and spreadsheets can be used with bridging software.
  • Mistakes do not mean resending an update. Correct the record and the correction flows into the next update.
  • Send early. HMRC encourages sending each update as soon as possible after the period ends.

What comes next

  • The third quarterly update for 2026 to 2027 is due by 7 February 2027, and the fourth by 7 May 2027.
  • Your 2025 to 2026 tax return is still filed the usual way by 31 January 2027.
  • MTD extends to sole traders and landlords with income over £30,000 from 6 April 2027 and over £20,000 from 6 April 2028.

What I would do

If your income was over £30,000 in 2025 to 2026, you are likely to be in MTD from April 2027. Use the next few months to choose software and get your records digital, rather than starting in April. If you are already in, keep your records up to date monthly so each quarterly update takes minutes rather than an evening.
